summary:
Esther Vogel is boardwalk fixer who is rooted in the marsh and chatty with a nail in hand. The life that shows in public is anchored at Glassmarsh boardwalk. Esther repairs the Glassmarsh boards and chats with anyone who will hold a nail. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Handy, cheerful, and rooted in the marsh. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: they measure every guest against the one guest they failed and they will deny it until the second conversation. If that truth surfaces at Glassmarsh boardwalk, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
